body:
Concentrated triage batch: `finding` → `pm:queue` + `domain:ui`, Task, S — post-#3909, the 10 `$filter: […] as any` casts in `ValueDataSource.test.ts` are redundant and actively erase the type-surface evidence these fixtures would otherwise provide (the file is the repo's fullest enumeration of the AST array forms). Delete the casts; if any assignment fails to compile bare, that is a real narrowing gap in #3909's union — report it rather than re-adding the cast.

---
_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

Claim: `domain:ui` execution seat, session `8ca04858-ea8e-5b85-9182-de59aa49e00c`, branch `claude/issue-6001-drop-redundant-filter-casts`.

## Blocker is dead — verified, not assumed

Body carries `Blocked-by: #3909`. Checked: #3909 is **closed/completed**, closed by **merged PR #5999**. Read `packages/types/src/data.ts` on `main` directly — the slot now reads:

```ts
$filter?: Record<string, any> | FilterArray;
```

`FilterArray` is bound from `@objectstack/spec/data`. The union is on the branch point. Nothing is waiting.

## Fence

**Exactly one file:** `packages/core/src/adapters/__tests__/ValueDataSource.test.ts`

Do not edit `packages/types/`, the spec package, or any other file. If the work appears to require touching anything outside that one path, **stop and report** rather than crossing — that is a signal my order is wrong, not that the fence is.

## The change

Delete the 10 redundant `as any` casts at lines 168, 177, 185, 194, 202, 210, 219, 227, 234, 241. The card's own instruction, quoted verbatim and not translated:

> 删掉这 10 处 `as any`，跑 `pnpm --filter @object-ui/core type-check` 确认无需替代 cast。**不要**换成别的断言或加宽任何东西 —— 这些值本来就合法，直接裸写即可。

⛔ Do not substitute a different assertion, do not widen any type, do not add a helper, do not touch the runtime assertions. The values are already legal; write them bare.

**If any one cast will not come off bare**, the standing triage instruction on this card governs — stop and report it as a real narrowing gap in the union, do **not** re-add the cast and do not work around it:

> if any assignment fails to compile bare, that is a real narrowing gap in #3909's union — report it rather than re-adding the cast.

Line 241 (`$filter: [] as any`) is the likeliest candidate, being the degenerate empty-array form. Report it; don't patch around it.

## A premise in the card that I believe is false — measure it, don't take my word

The card justifies itself with a second claim: that once the casts are gone the fixtures become compile-time evidence, because *"一旦有人把该槽位收窄回记录形式，这个文件会转红"*.

I think that is wrong, and the source is #3909's own landed text. The doc comment PR #5999 wrote into `data.ts` states, as a measurement:

> Note the declaration does not *narrow* anything: `Record<string, any>` already structurally accepts arrays (they satisfy its string index), so the union documents the shapes that were always accepted rather than admitting new ones.

#3909's body says the same and cites `tsc --strict` exit 0. If that holds, then narrowing the slot back to the bare record form would **not** turn this file red, and the casts were removable before #3909 ever landed.

So: **do not assert the "turns red" claim in the PR body.** Settle it by measurement instead, as a local uncommitted probe:

1. Commit the cast deletion first.
2. Predict the direction out loud before looking.
3. Locally narrow the slot in `packages/types/src/data.ts` back to `Record<string, any>` — prove the mutation landed on disk (anchored grep plus a `git hash-object` blob-hash difference, not an exit code).
4. Run the type-check and observe whether this test file goes red.
5. Restore, and prove the restore **by observation** — `git diff HEAD` empty **and** the blob hash back to its original value. Never by exit code.

Report the observed direction either way. If it stays green, the deletion is still correct (the casts are genuinely redundant) but its value is "removes a misleading no-op cast", not "adds a type-surface witness" — and the PR body must say the true one. A zero here needs a positive control: if nothing goes red, show something that *does* go red under the same probe shape, or the zero is NOT MEASURED rather than green.

The probe touches a file outside the fence. That is authorised **only** as a local, uncommitted, proven-restored measurement — it must never appear in a commit or the diff.

## Verification before pushing

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/core type-check` — green, with no replacement casts.
- Run the test file itself; the runtime assertions must be untouched and still passing.
- Anchored grep: 10 occurrences of the cast before, 0 after, in that one file.
- Changeset: test-only change. Follow the repo's changeset policy and let the `Changeset Declaration` gate rule whether one is owed — do not pre-empt it in either direction.

Draft PR, `Fixes #6001`.

⚠️ Correction to the dispatch order above — three fragments were damaged in transit. **Read these in place of the corresponding lines in that comment.** The order is otherwise unchanged and still governs.

The generic type argument was stripped from `Record< string, any >` in three places, leaving a bare `Record` that reads as complete but is not. Restating each with spaces inside the brackets so it survives:

**1. The slot on `main`** (the fenced block under "Blocker is dead") should read:

```ts
$filter?: Record< string, any > | FilterArray;
```

not `$filter?: Record | FilterArray;`, which is not a type.

**2. The quotation from the doc comment PR #5999 landed in `packages/types/src/data.ts`** should read:

> Note the declaration does not *narrow* anything: `Record< string, any >` already structurally accepts arrays (they satisfy its string index), so the union documents the shapes that were always accepted rather than admitting new ones.

**3. Probe step 3** should read: locally narrow the slot in `packages/types/src/data.ts` back to `Record< string, any >` — i.e. drop the `| FilterArray` arm, leaving the record form alone. As written it said "back to `Record`", which is not executable.

Nothing else changes: same one-file fence, same 10 line numbers, same ⛔ on substituting assertions or widening, same stop-and-report rule if a cast will not come off bare, same requirement that the probe stay local, uncommitted and proven-restored.

Note for the lane: this is the sanitizer failure the protocol warns about — a fenced code block and backticks are both **not** protection, and what survived was a plausible-looking shorter string rather than an obvious hole. The spelling with spaces inside the angle brackets is what the surrounding issue bodies use, and it is what survives.

ACCEPT — PR #6630, flipped ready and armed for the queue.

**Entry qualification, on head `234415d6`:** 29 checks, and 29 returned against `total_count: 29` so no page was silently dropped. **26 success, 3 skipped, zero failures, zero cancelled, zero still running.** Every check green, not merely the required subset. The three skips are `dependabot` and the two coverage matrix jobs, all skipped by their own conditions rather than by anything in this diff.

**Fence held, verified against the file list rather than the report's word:** exactly two files — `packages/core/src/adapters/__tests__/ValueDataSource.test.ts` and the changeset. `packages/types/` appears in no commit on the branch, so the probe really was local and uncommitted.

**The change is what was ordered and nothing more:** ten casts deleted, nothing substituted — no replacement assertion, no widened type, no helper — and every runtime assertion untouched. The file's other eleven `as any` are unrelated record-shape assertions and are still there.

**The card's second premise is refuted, and the PR says the true thing instead.** Measured, not argued: narrowing the slot back to the record form leaves the type-check at exit 0 with zero errors mentioning this file. The zero carries a positive control in the identical probe shape — a slot that genuinely excludes arrays produces 10 errors at exactly the ten lines — so it is a measurement, not a blind apparatus.

The part that makes that measurement valid is the part I did not order. `packages/core/tsconfig.test.json` sets empty `paths` on purpose, so the program reads `packages/types/dist/data.d.ts`, not the source. A probe that edited only the source — which is what my order literally asked for — would have changed nothing the checker sees and returned a meaningless green. The dev checked the apparatus first, rebuilt, and proved the mutation reached `dist` before trusting any reading. My order was under-specified; the work was not.

**Two corrections to this card that should not be re-derived by whoever reads it next:**

1. The "un-cast fixtures become compile-time evidence" claim is **false**. Narrowing the slot back does not turn this file red.
2. Therefore `Blocked-by: #3909` was **never real**. Since the record form already accepts arrays structurally, these ten casts were removable before #3909 / PR #5999 ever landed.

The merge value is the smaller true one: an `as any` at a site where the value is already legal is a no-op that reads as a live constraint, and a reader who trusts it concludes the array form is illegal here — which is how the tolerant consumer AGENTS.md #0.1 forbids gets written. The changeset carries that correction too, so it survives into the changelog rather than only living in this thread.

Also settled on the record: the one-file fence versus the gate-mandated changeset was **my** contradiction, not the dev's judgement call. A fence enumerates the *source* files a change may touch; gate-mandated artifacts are carried by the gate's ruling.

Closure will be confirmed from `closed_by_pull_requests` after the merge, not assumed from the `Fixes` line.
